name: PRINCIPLES

paper.title: PRINCIPLES: Synthetic Strategy Memory for Proactive Dialogue Agents

construction.unit: principle: 'When [situation], you should [strategy], rather than [failed strategy], because [reason]'
construction.kept_as: LLM-derived lesson in a fixed template; the When clause is also stored separately
construction.processing: offline self-play; a turn whose critic reward rises yields a principle; a turn that does not rise is revised and re-simulated (up to 3 tries) and a success after revision yields a contrastive principle
construction.writer: LLM prompted with the dialogue, the successful turn and any failed tries

organization.structure: flat set of principles per domain
organization.index: embedding of the When clause (text-embedding-ada-002, L2 distance)

retrieval.selection: top-k = 3; each retrieved principle is rewritten by an LLM to fit the current dialogue

use.context: the reinterpreted principles replace the strategy slot of the agent's response prompt
use.reasoning: one reply per turn; no separate strategy-planning call at inference

classify.note: The LLM reinterpretation rewrites the 3 retrieved principles but does not choose among them.

stages.ingestion: Offline self-play on training dialogues: an agent, a user simulator and a critic LLM play out conversations started from the first turn of a training dialogue (50 simulations per dataset, up to 10 turns).
stages.construction: After each turn the critic's averaged reward is compared with the previous turn. If it rose, an LLM writes a When/should/because principle from the turn. If not, the strategy is revised from the failed tries, the turn is replayed from the same state (up to 3 tries), and a success yields a When/should/rather than/because principle.
stages.organization: About 100 principles per domain in one flat set; the When clause is embedded for search.
stages.retrieval: At each turn the dialogue so far is embedded and the 3 principles whose When clauses are closest (L2, FAISS) are retrieved; an LLM rewrites each to fit the current dialogue.
stages.answer: The reinterpreted principles serve as the dialogue strategy in the agent's reply prompt (one short sentence per turn).
stages.learning: No parameter updates; memory is built from simulated experience only.

summary: A strategy memory for proactive dialogue built by offline self-play: turns that raise the critic's reward, or that succeed after backtracking and revision, are turned into When / should / rather than / because principles, retrieved by situation and reinterpreted to guide each reply.
notes:
Venue: EMNLP 2025 Findings (arXiv comment; ACL Anthology 2025.findings-emnlp.1164, pages 21329-21368). PDF read: arXiv v1 (22 Sep 2025). Code: kimnamssya/Principles at 8a82a1e2 (2025-09-23), linked from the project page on Hugging Face Spaces named in the abstract; it holds the self-play environment, the PRINCIPLES agent, prompts and data splits, but no derived principle files and no baseline implementations.
DESIGN: §2, §3.1-3.3, §4.1, App. A, E, F.1; code src/run.py, src/agent.py, src/env.py, scripts/run_ours.sh. Classified as procedural memory: stored items are reusable dialogue strategies, not facts about a user. management 'none': no update or deletion after offline construction (an online, success-only construction variant is reported in Table 6).

sources.code_note: Authors' repository, linked from the project page cited in the abstract. Pinned at the latest commit 8a82a1e2 (2025-09-23), one day after arXiv v1. The released run script defaults every model to gpt-4o-mini, while the paper uses gpt-4o as user simulator and critic; the derived principle files (resources/principles/) and the prompts for the unstructured ablation are not included.

headline: Memory is a set of ~100 strategy rules written by an LLM during offline self-play, not records of the user or the conversation.
Only the When clause is matched; the whole rule is then rewritten by an LLM for the current dialogue and handed to the agent as its strategy.
Failed turns are replayed from the same state with revised strategies, so many rules carry a 'rather than' contrast with what failed.

units.name: Principle
units.role: one reusable strategy lesson from a simulated turn

fields.name: when
fields.what: the situation, tied to the user's last utterance

fields.name: raw principle
fields.what: the full When / should / (rather than) / because sentence

fields.name: should / rather than / because
fields.what: parsed parts of the principle, saved but not read separately

fields.name: rationale
fields.what: the LLM's explanation of why the strategy worked

write.how: planner LLM writes a one-sentence strategy, the agent replies with it, the user simulator answers, the critic scores the dialogue 10 times and the mapped scores are averaged
write.src: paper §2, App. F.1; code env.py L128-L161, L282-L296

write.how: if the reward is higher than the previous turn's, an LLM writes a When/should/because principle from the dialogue and the turn
otherwise an LLM proposes a new strategy from the failed tries, the turn is removed and replayed from the same state
if a replay raises the reward, an LLM compares it with the failed tries and writes When/should/rather than/because
after 3 failed tries the dialogue continues from the best-scoring try and no principle is written
write.note: the paper's Algorithm 1 keeps the original turn instead
write.src: code run.py L119-L128; paper App. A

write.how: at test time the When clauses are embedded into a FAISS store with the full principle as metadata
write.out: about 100 principles from 50 simulations per domain (Fig. 7 shows 47 from success, 37 from failure)

read.input: the dialogue so far, as 'Role: text' lines
read.how: embedding similarity, L2 distance in FAISS
one LLM call per principle rewrites it in the same format for the current dialogue
read.src: paper §3.2 eq. 13, Fig. 18; code agent.py L154-L186

read.how: the rewritten principles, joined by newlines, fill the {action} slot of the agent prompt; the agent answers in one short sentence

answer_context.sees: the dialogue so far plus 3 reinterpreted principles as the requested strategy
answer_context.format: role-play prompt '... reply with only one short and succinct sentence using the following dialogue strategy: {action}', with the principles as {action}

compression.basis: Only the principle length is reported: 62.93 tokens on average for GPT-4o-built principles on ESConv (Table 7); no source length is given.

paper_vs_code.paper: gpt-4o as user simulator and critic (§3.3); principle source model GPT-4o (Table 7)
paper_vs_code.code: run_ours.sh sets agent, user, critic, principle and reinterpretation models to gpt-4o-mini

paper_vs_code.paper: Algorithm 1 continues from the original failed turn

paper_vs_code.code: next_action returns a (text, '') tuple that is placed directly in the {action} slot

paper_vs_code.paper: status compares r_t with r_{t-1} at every turn
paper_vs_code.code: comparison starts only when two rewards exist, so the first turn of a simulation never yields a principle

open_questions: The best k differs by task (9 for ESConv, 3 for P4G in Fig. 10) and the main results use 3; ESConv at k = 9 (80.0) would exceed Table 1's 73.85.
Table 3 does not separate the value of the stored content from the value of reinterpretation per turn: w/o Reinterpretation and w/o Structured give the same ExTES SR (83.85).
Success of a turn is judged by one LLM critic that also decides the final success rate, so principles are optimised for the evaluator used to score them.

components.role: Plans and revises strategies in self-play

components.model: GPT-4o by default (Table 7 also tries Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Llama-3.1-8B)

discussion.takeaway: Strategy rules mined from an LLM's own simulated successes and repaired failures, stored as situation-indexed principles, beat prompted and trained strategy planners on emotional-support and persuasion self-play without any training.

claims.evidence: SR 73.85 ESConv, 86.15 ExTES, 59.17 P4G+ vs best baselines 58.46, 71.54, 53.33; P4G 95.00 vs PPDPP 96.67. Table 1
Highest macro F1, weighted F1 and entropy on ESConv (10.52 / 17.67 / 1.21) and P4G (14.96 / 24.30 / 2.67). Table 2

claims.claim: No training is needed and cost stays low.
claims.evidence: PPDPP training costs about 11.5x more (Fig. 3); DPDP 18.07x training and 3.07x inference cost for 79.23 vs 73.85 SR on ESConv. Table 4

claims.claim: Lessons from both success and failure are needed.
claims.evidence: Both sources together beat either alone on ExTES and ESConv. Fig. 8

claims.claim: All four parts of the template matter.
claims.evidence: ESConv SR 73.85 full, 62.31 without 'rather than', 64.00 without 'because'. Table 5

claims.claim: Principles can also be built online.
claims.evidence: ESConv SR 66.15 online (success only) vs 73.85 offline. Table 6

limits: Retrieval uses L2 embedding distance between the dialogue and the When clause, which can miss fine contextual differences; reinterpretation may not fix very specific or ambiguous situations.
Planning is turn by turn with no explicit long-term goal, so the agent may chase short-term reward in tasks such as negotiation.
Principles are not reviewed by experts; no clinical claims are made for emotional-support use.
reading: All scores come from self-play with an LLM user simulator and an LLM critic (gpt-4o); the same kind of critic reward also decides which turns become principles, so the memory is shaped by the evaluator.
The paper states that user simulator and critic are gpt-4o but does not state the agent backbone for PRINCIPLES and the baselines in Table 1; the released script uses gpt-4o-mini for all roles.
Figure 10 shows ESConv SR 80.0 at k = 9 against 73.9 at the default k = 3, and P4G 95.0 at k = 3; results are sensitive to k and the main table uses one fixed value.
Figure 9 shows P4G+ SR 60.0 at 25 simulations and 59.2 at 50, so '50 is optimal' holds for ExTES (86.2) but not clearly for P4G+.
In Table 3, the 'w/o Structured' and 'w/o Reinterpretation' rows are identical on both datasets (83.85 / 56.67).
Table 7: principles built with Llama-3.1-8B score higher on ESConv (86.15) than those built with GPT-4o (73.85).
The paper cites Ask-an-Expert as Zhang et al. 2024b in the text but lists it as 2023 in the references and Fig. 28 caption.

abstract.text: PRINCIPLES targets strategy planning in proactive dialogue such as emotional support and persuasion, where fixed strategy sets cover too little, LLMs favour a few strategies, and trained planners are costly. The method runs offline self-play on training dialogues and converts turns that improved the critic's score, or that succeeded after backtracking and revision, into structured principles. At inference, principles matching the current situation are retrieved, adapted to the dialogue and used to guide the agent, with no training. It outperforms prompted and trained baselines on ESConv, ExTES, P4G and an extended P4G+.
